skill.nightborn.core.thick_blood.descrip: A tenth more health with each rank
skill.nightborn.core.grave_strength.desc: Your blows land harder with each rank
skill.nightborn.core.blood_rush.descript: Burn blood for a short burst of speed and strength
skill.nightborn.core.vanish.description: Vanish in smoke and reappear a few steps the way you are moving, or behind you if you stand still
skill.nightborn.core.night_eyes.descript: See in the dark at any hour. The second rank halves blindness and darkness. The third sees through Grave Fog
skill.nightborn.core.blood_healing.descr: Burn blood to heal over a few moments
skill.nightborn.core.iron_grip.descripti: Victims break free less often, you feed faster and you shake off snares and nets sooner, more with each rank
skill.nightborn.core.deep_veins.descript: Two more blood points on the bar with each rank
skill.nightborn.core.unbroken.descriptio: Downed for less time, and you rise with more health
skill.nightborn.core.sanguine_mastery.de: Every power is ready again sooner
skill.nightborn.noble.noble_blood.descri: Chooses the Noble bloodline. Old pride hardens your skin, more with each rank
skill.nightborn.beast.beast_blood.descri: Chooses the Beast bloodline. You land on your feet from higher falls
skill.nightborn.beast.bat_form.descripti: Turn into a bat and fly, and use it again to turn back. Flying drains blood, and sun, garlic, holy water or a heavy blow force you back
skill.nightborn.beast.beast_claws.descri: Your bare hands strike harder: two more damage at the first rank and one more with each rank after
skill.nightborn.beast.swift_prowl.descri: A tenth more speed with each rank
skill.nightborn.beast.hear_heartbeats.de: For a few moments the living nearby show through walls, redder the more blood they hold
skill.nightborn.beast.pounce.description: Leap onto the creature you look at and pin it down. You can bite a pinned creature without sneaking
skill.nightborn.beast.blood_frenzy.descr: Faster and harder hitting for a while, but your blood drains twice as fast. Each kill makes it last longer. On the bar, it wakes by itself when you are close to death
skill.nightborn.beast.night_terror.descr: Become a great winged beast. You fly, your claws tear deep and blows hurt you half as much. Your roar staggers those nearby. You cannot feed or use other powers, and whatever drives a bat back to its shape drives you back too
skill.nightborn.beast.apex_predator.desc: Beast powers cost one less blood and come back sooner
skill.nightborn.occult.occult_blood.desc: Chooses the Occult bloodline. Your reach stretches a little further with each rank
skill.nightborn.hunter.tracking.descript: For a short time, sense the direction of the nearest vampire
skill.nightborn.hunter.weathered.descrip: Hard years on the road toughen your hide, more with each rank
skill.nightborn.hunter.second_wind.descr: Draw a hard breath and push on, faster and harder to hurt for a short time
skill.nightborn.hunter.clear_eyes.descri: Blindness and darkness lift from you sooner
skill.nightborn.hunter.bind_wounds.descr: Bind your own wounds and heal over a few moments
skill.nightborn.hunter.sure_footing.desc: You land on your feet from higher falls
skill.nightborn.hunter.unyielding.descri: Blows and charges throw you back less
skill.nightborn.hunter.old_hand.descript: Years on the hunt make every power ready again sooner
skill.nightborn.hunter.bite_ward.descrip: Break free of a vampire's bite sooner, and suffer less weakness and sickness from it
skill.nightborn.hunter.faith.description: Crucifixes and holy water work stronger in your hands
skill.nightborn.hunter.iron_will.descrip: A vampire's stare holds you less
skill.nightborn.seeker.keen_tracking.des: Tracking reaches further and lasts longer. At the last rank, fresh blood trails show
skill.nightborn.seeker.sixth_sense.descr: You are warned, and which way, when a vampire watches, stalks or hunts you
skill.nightborn.seeker.soft_step.descrip: You make less noise in a vampire's house
skill.nightborn.seeker.read_the_scene.de: Read a victim, a coffin or a kill: the age of the vampire behind it, its bloodlines and the way it went
skill.nightborn.seeker.mark_quarry.descr: Mark one creature in sight. It shows through walls, a marked vampire takes more harm from you, and its trail stays for Tracking
skill.nightborn.seeker.grave_listener.de: While you sneak, you hear sleeping vampires nearby and see their shapes through walls
skill.nightborn.seeker.true_sight.descri: For a few seconds, see every vampire nearby through walls, even one that is hidden
skill.nightborn.seeker.revelation.descri: Mark every vampire far around you for yourself and the humans beside you, and strip away their veils, mist and glamour
Seeker powers come back sooner, and your allies strike harder at a vampire you have marked
skill.nightborn.trapper.field_craft.desc: Your traps are set a quarter faster with each rank, and a vampire cannot see them from more than 6, then 4, then 2 blocks away
skill.nightborn.trapper.snare.descriptio: Set a hidden snare on the ground you look at. A vampire who steps on it is pinned down, but a bat or mist passes over it. Two can be set at once
skill.nightborn.trapper.bait.description: Spill blood on the ground you look at. Hungry vampires nearby come to it, and a vampire close by smells it
skill.nightborn.trapper.net_shot.descrip: Fire a net. A vampire it catches is dragged down out of the air and out of bat shape, and cannot leave the ground for a while
skill.nightborn.trapper.quick_hands.desc: One more snare can be set at once with each rank
skill.nightborn.trapper.trap_sense.descr: You see your own traps and your allies' traps outlined, and never set one off yourself
skill.nightborn.trapper.silver_edge.desc: Your snares and nets cut with silver and your flash traps burn hotter, more with each rank
skill.nightborn.trapper.flash_trap.descr: Set a trap on the ground you look at. When a vampire comes near, it bursts in holy light that burns like the sun and blinds. One can be set at once
skill.nightborn.trapper.killing_ground.d: Mark a wide circle around you for a while. Traps inside reset the moment they spring, and a vampire inside cannot vanish, shadow step, take bat form or turn to mist
skill.nightborn.trapper.master_trapper.d: Trapper powers come back sooner, and your blows hurt a pinned vampire more
skill.nightborn.faithful.mend.descriptio: Pray over the wounded. You and every human close by are healed at once
skill.nightborn.faithful.rebuke.descript: With a crucifix in hand or worn, throw back every vampire in front of you and stop their powers for a moment
skill.nightborn.faithful.blessing.descri: Bless your weapon, or that of an ally you look at. For a while it strikes as if coated in holy water, with no limit on its hits
skill.nightborn.faithful.grace.descripti: Your healing prayers heal a quarter more with each rank
skill.nightborn.faithful.blood_fire.desc: Cut yourself and set your weapon alight. It burns bright, deals fire damage, sets a vampire alight and stops it healing while it burns
skill.nightborn.faithful.sanctuary.descr: Pray for a while. Humans around you slowly heal, are freed from a vampire's stare and cannot be stared still or cowed
skill.nightborn.faithful.consecrate.desc: Bless the ground around you for a while. A vampire on it is weakened as by a crucifix, cast out of bat and winged shape, and cannot levitate, vanish or take bat form
skill.nightborn.faithful.judgement.descr: Call down a pillar of holy light where you look. It burns a vampire inside like the sun and heals a human
Faithful powers come back sooner, and your healing prayers also lift Weakness
skill.nightborn.slayer.sidestep.descript: Dash a few blocks the way you are moving, untouchable for a breath. A vampire whose blow you slip staggers
skill.nightborn.slayer.stake_throw.descr: Hurl a stake from your pack. It wounds, staggers a vampire and knocks it out of the air, and can be picked up again. A thrown stake never stakes
skill.nightborn.slayer.riposte.descripti: Raise your guard for half a second. A vampire that leaps, pounces, dashes or steps at you through it is thrown back and staggered
skill.nightborn.slayer.quick_shot.descri: Fire a loaded crossbow at once, with no time to raise it
skill.nightborn.slayer.heartstrike.descr: Lunge at a vampire with a stake in hand. One that is snared, netted, pinned or caught off guard, and badly hurt, is downed at once. Any other takes a heavier stake's blow
skill.nightborn.slayer.last_stand.descri: When you are close to death, for a few seconds you cannot be bitten or mesmerised and you hit harder
skill.nightborn.slayer.onslaught.descrip: For a few seconds you strike twice as fast and harder against vampires. A badly hurt vampire you strike is downed, and must still be staked. An ancient never falls to it
skill.nightborn.slayer.slayers_calm.desc: Slayer powers come back sooner, and a dodge that staggers gives Sidestep back at once

nightborn.journal.hunter.name: The Hunter's Journal
nightborn.journal.hunter.landing: Field book of the guild. Handed down, added to by many hands, never finished. Each who swears the oath is given a copy, and its pages open as you learn the trade.$(br2)Lose it and any Guild Master will hand you another. He will not be pleased.
The oath, the ranks and the work that pays.
nightborn.journal.hunter.category.quarry: What it is, where it sleeps and how it is ended.
nightborn.journal.hunter.category.arms.d: Wood, silver, garlic and blessed water. Carry all four.
nightborn.journal.hunter.oath.1: You have staked one of them and sworn before a Guild Master. That makes you a hunter of the guild. Nothing counted before the oath. What you learn, the skills you take, your rank and your contracts all begin from it. The ones you killed before were practice.
nightborn.journal.hunter.oath.2: Guild Masters keep the camps in open country and walk with the hunting parties. Go to one and speak to him as you would to a trader. He sells gear, writes contracts, tells you your rank and knows where the nearest vampire house lies.$(br2)$(o)No vampire may swear. Do not vouch for one.$()
nightborn.journal.hunter.ranks.1: Four ranks: Initiate, Hunter, Veteran, Master. Each asks enough in the guild's reckoning of what you have learned, and a deed besides. A Hunter has staked an adult or older. A Veteran has staked the last of a household. A Master has ended the Eldest. A deed done early still stands.
nightborn.journal.hunter.ranks.2: Rank makes you harder to kill, and your blows fall heavier on vampires. It opens the deepest skills, better stock from the Guild Master and harder contracts. No rank is ever taken back, and its mark is drawn beside your name where all can see it.
nightborn.journal.hunter.paths.1: Every vampire staked teaches you something. Learn enough and you may take a new skill ($(k:key.nightborn.skills)). All hunters begin with the core. Its first skill is Tracking, which turns you toward the nearest vampire for a short while. The rest of it hardens you for the road.
nightborn.journal.hunter.paths.2: Past the core the trade splits four ways: Trapper, Faithful, Slayer, Seeker. Your first skill in a path binds you to it, and once you are bound to two the others are shut. Skills you must call on sit ready to hand ($(k:key.nightborn.power_1) and on). They cost you nothing, but each needs time before it answers again.
nightborn.journal.hunter.contracts.1: A Guild Master writes contracts on paper: stake so many, stake an elder, or clear a house by staking the last of it. Each paper keeps its own count. When it is done, carry it back in your hand and give it to any Guild Master. He pays in emeralds, silver and gear, and the work adds to your reckoning.
nightborn.journal.hunter.vampires.1: Only a stake and the sun end a vampire. Remember it. Blade, bolt, fire or fall, any other wound stops short and leaves it downed: fallen and helpless for half a minute. Put a stake in it then and it is finished.
nightborn.journal.hunter.vampires.2: Leave it lying and it gets up and runs, and for a while after only a stake or the sun will touch it. I lost one that way at Michaelmas.$(br2)A staking adds to your reckoning, and adds more the older the thing was: fledgling, adult, elder, ancient.
nightborn.journal.hunter.vampires.3: The bite can carry a sickness that makes you one of them. Cure it before it runs its course: eat a golden apple while under Weakness, or drink holy water. Once you have turned there is no cure.$(br2)$(m)I feel well enough.$()$(br)$(o)He did not. We staked him on the Tuesday.$()
nightborn.journal.hunter.vampires.4: In a fight they read you. Run, and one springs after you or steps out of the dark at your back. Wind up a blow or draw a bow, and it is gone in smoke, or it has you fast by the eyes. If you are already slowed it will not waste another charm on you. Fall low and it comes in for the finish. Wounded, it vanishes the way it was already going, and the sun sends it leaping for the nearest shade.$(br2)$(o)Never turn your back. W.B.$()
nightborn.journal.hunter.weaknesses.1: One Garlic String weakens every vampire within eight paces, and more strings weaken more. Garlic in the hand, or touched, weakens far worse. A crucifix in either hand weakens and slows any vampire within six paces that can see it, and none of them can bite you while you hold it.
nightborn.journal.hunter.weaknesses.2: Holy water burns them and leaves them weak a while. Silver cuts deeper than iron. Weakness from different things adds together, and a weakened vampire stoops and staggers.$(br2)$(o)Garlic and crosses never stopped one breaking down a door. Bolt it anyway.$()
nightborn.journal.hunter.households.1: They keep households. Castles in the dark forests. Crypts under village churches. Ruined manors. Lairs off the deep caves. And the great castles on the highest mountains, which we do not speak of after dark. Fog hangs about every one, thickest at its heart.
nightborn.journal.hunter.households.2: By day they sleep in coffins. Lift a lid and the sun reaches whatever lies inside. A castle is ruled by a vampire lord, who calls his court and a swarm of bats to his side. Before you go looking, ask a Guild Master for news of the nearest house. A Master can also send a proven Hunter there himself, by rite, for a tithe of emeralds. You are set down at its door, and for a few breaths nothing can touch you. $(o)Strike first and that grace is gone. He will not do it twice in one day. T.$()
nightborn.journal.hunter.the_eldest.1: Each kind of house but the mountain castle keeps a relic: a Castle Signet, a Crypt Reliquary, a Manor Locket, a Lair Fang. One of each makes a Ritual Altar. Set a chalice of blood on it at night and the Eldest comes, with every power of every bloodline. Be sure you want it to.
nightborn.journal.hunter.the_eldest.2: It fights inside a ring of red fog in three shapes, each worse than the last. Every blow shows itself before it lands. Break the third and it is downed, and you have a short while to stake it. Every hunter who struck it is paid in full. One waits atop every mountain castle besides.
nightborn.journal.hunter.stakes_and_silv: A Wooden Stake is two sticks: light, quick, and it never sweeps. Silver ore lies underground, rarer than iron, and wants an iron pickaxe. Silver makes a sword, an axe and a stake tip. It wears out sooner than iron and hits as hard, and it cuts a vampire deeper.
A crossbow will take stake bolts, silver bolts, holy water bolts and Garlic Bombs. A silver-tipped stake is stake and silver at once.$(br2)$(o)Whittle a spare. Then another.$()
nightborn.journal.hunter.holy_water.1: Brew a bottle of water with a silver nugget, or pay a cleric an emerald to bless one. It can be made to drink, to throw or to linger where it falls. It harms nothing but a vampire, and a mouthful cures the bite sickness.
nightborn.journal.hunter.holy_water.2: Holy water or garlic can be worked onto any weapon or shot at the crafting table. On a weapon it lasts for so many blows on vampires or for so long, whichever ends first. On a bolt or an arrow it lasts until loosed.
nightborn.journal.hunter.garlic.1: Garlic grows wild on the plains and about villages, and it can be farmed. Eaten raw it stays hunger a little. Braid it into Garlic Strings and hang them where vampires walk. Or load Garlic Bombs into a crossbow: each bursts into a cloud that weakens every vampire inside it.
nightborn.journal.vampire.name: The Vampire's Journal
nightborn.journal.vampire.landing: I began this ledger the night I woke changed, and I have kept it longer than your family has had a name. Now it is yours. Its pages open as you learn what you have become.$(br2)Lose it and an Old Blood Font will return it to you. It has done as much for me, more than once.
nightborn.journal.vampire.category.chang: What you are now, and the few things that can still end you.
nightborn.journal.vampire.category.growt: The years, the bloodlines and what each of them gives.
nightborn.journal.vampire.category.house: Where you sleep, who serves you and who is coming to kill you.
nightborn.journal.vampire.what_you_are.1: You are twice as hard to kill as you were, and your bare hands strike harder. After dark you see without a lamp, run faster and leap higher. Will it, and you hang a pace above the floor ($(k:key.nightborn.levitate)). No bed will have you now. You sleep in a coffin or not at all.
nightborn.journal.vampire.what_you_are.2: Only two things end our kind: a stake, and the sun. Any other wound, however grave, leaves you fallen and helpless for half a minute. Then you rise and slip away, and for a little while nothing but the sun and the stake can touch you. I have risen so more often than I care to count.
nightborn.journal.vampire.blood.1: Hunger is thirst now, and only blood answers it. It ebbs slowly while you are still, and quickly when you run, fight or call on your gifts. Keep more than half full and your wounds close by themselves. Bread and meat, milk and potions give you nothing and come straight back up. Garlic is the worst of them.
nightborn.journal.vampire.blood.2: To feed, sneak close with an empty hand, take hold and keep hold ($(k:key.use)). Let go and it lives. Hold on to the end and you drain it dry. Prey will sometimes tear free and turn on you, and a villager who sees you at it runs for the bell. I learned long ago to dine without company.
nightborn.journal.vampire.blood.3: Go without and you starve. You weaken, your gifts fail you, and at the last your own body begins to waste. It will not end you. Nothing so merciful. Any blood at all stops it.
nightborn.journal.vampire.feeding_well.1: Not all blood is equal. Beasts are thin fare. Villagers and their outlaw cousins are better. Best is one of the living who walks the world as freely as you do. Fresh is worth more than bottled. Even so, hold an empty glass bottle in your off hand as you feed and it fills, against the lean nights, though you drink none of it yourself.
nightborn.journal.vampire.feeding_well.2: Fresh blood leaves something of its owner in you for a short while. A horse lends its speed, a wolf its nose for prey. A villager quickens your healing, an illager gives strength, and a witch hardens you against potions. In a fight, when an enemy is close to falling, bite. It ends the matter.
nightborn.journal.vampire.the_sun.1: The sun sets you alight the moment it finds you, and burns for as long as you stand in it. That fire kills, fallen or standing, and no armour or potion turns it. Shade, rain, water, a shut coffin and an open parasol do. Flames that follow you into the shade will only lay you low.
nightborn.journal.vampire.the_sun.2: A parasol is sticks and wool, and it lets you walk at noon. Open it in either hand. Only the sun wears it thin, and you burn the instant it breaks or folds. Running, rising off the ground, taking the bat's shape or taking a blow folds it. Mend it with wool. I am never without one.
nightborn.journal.vampire.weaknesses.1: Garlic hung on a string saps you from eight paces, and every string more saps you further. Garlic touched or held is far worse. A crucifix raised within six paces weakens and slows you, and you cannot bite the one who holds it. Blessed water burns and weakens. Silver bites deeper than iron.
nightborn.journal.vampire.weaknesses.2: A stake wounds worse than any blade, and if it finds you while you lie fallen, that is the end. Should you wake again after a staking, you wake lesser: a tenth of all the skill you had earned is gone. Weakness alone never wounds you, but it gathers, and while it is on you your gifts will not answer.
nightborn.journal.vampire.age.1: You begin a fledgling. Each stage after it wants nights enough lived as one of us and blood enough drunk, and then a deed to mark the passage. A fledgling becomes an adult by draining a villager or an illager. An adult becomes an elder by ending a Guild Master.
nightborn.journal.vampire.age.2: Each stage makes you harder to kill and heavier of hand, and you hold more blood and spend it more slowly. It opens the deepest skills, lets you keep a larger house and changes the colour your name is written in. It is never lost. Look to your skills ($(k:key.nightborn.skills)) to see your stage and what the next one asks.
nightborn.journal.vampire.bloodlines.1: Feeding teaches. Drink enough and you may take a new skill ($(k:key.nightborn.skills)). All of us share the core: Thick Blood, Grave Strength, Blood Rush and Vanish. Beyond it the blood divides three ways.
nightborn.journal.vampire.bloodlines.2: The Noble rules: it bends minds and keeps servants. The Beast hunts, with the bat's shape, claws and speed. The Occult conjures familiars, fog and shadow. Your first skill in a bloodline binds you to it. Bind yourself to two and the third is shut to you for good. Choose slowly. I did not.
nightborn.journal.vampire.bat_form.1: Those of the Beast can take the shape of a bat and fly wherever they look, faster at a sprint. Flight drinks blood, and when you run dry it throws you back into your own shape. Fly into the ground to land and crawl. Use the underside of anything solid to hang from it.
nightborn.journal.vampire.bat_form.2: A bat cannot strike, feed, put anything it carries to use or call on its other gifts. Direct sun, a heavy blow, blessed water or garlic close by will force you back into yourself. If that happens in the air, you fall. The eyes are little use. A bat hears the shape of a room rather than sees it: each footfall and each drip throws the walls back at you for a moment, then lets them go dark again.
nightborn.journal.vampire.servants.1: Any of us may take a grown villager into service with a Familiar's Contract: paper, a feather and a Blood Bottle. It works by day, carries between the chests you mark, trades in your name and guards your coffin. Pay it in emeralds. Loyalty that is not paid for does not last.
nightborn.journal.vampire.servants.2: A Noble can mesmerise a villager and sip from it, and it becomes a thrall that follows and fights for you. The Occult summon ghostly familiars. Go to any servant and speak to it as you would to a trader, and it will take your orders.
nightborn.journal.vampire.coffins.1: The coffin is your bed. Lie in it by day, from dawn to dusk, and if enough of our kind sleep, the day passes. The coffin you sleep in becomes yours. No hand but yours can break it, and it is where you wake should the worst befall you. Sneak and use it with an empty hand to lift or shut the lid.
nightborn.journal.vampire.coffins.2: A shut lid keeps out the sun and hides you from anyone who looks. An open one lets the sun in. Sneak as you set a coffin down and it stands upright, which I am told looks grander. I have always slept flat.
nightborn.journal.vampire.coffins.3: Lie down within the first hour after dawn and sleep through to dusk, or sleep while enough of us pass the day, and you wake rested: whole again, no blood spent in your sleep, and a little quicker and stronger until dawn. A coffin of your own house rests you better.
nightborn.journal.vampire.houses.1: An adult or older may found a house: lie in your own coffin while you lead no other, or in the coffin of a fallen household's head. The founder is its lord. To invite a younger wanderer of our kind, go and speak to them. The rest answer only to a full gold chalice, offered in the hand.
nightborn.journal.vampire.houses.2: The older the lord, the more the house can hold. Its members keep the place, sleep in its coffins, carry blood home and defend it.$(br2)$(o)/house tells you which house is yours and where it stands.$()
nightborn.journal.vampire.hunters.1: The guild exists to kill us. Its camps stand in open country and its parties walk the roads behind a Guild Master. When a village grows frightened enough to send for them, a party camps beside it and stays for as long as the fear lasts. Let the fear die and they strike their tents by first light at the latest and move on. They strike on sight, with stakes, crossbows, crucifixes and blessed water, and they finish whoever they bring down. A Guild Master can set a hunter down at our very door in a moment, wrapped in a light that nothing breaks for a few breaths. Wait it out. No Guild Master will trade with you. Do not ask. I asked, once.
nightborn.journal.vampire.hunters.2: Nor are they fools once it comes to blows. Run from one and a net finds your legs. Come at one and you may step in the snare he laid at his feet. Take to the air and a net or a thrown stake brings you down. Gather yourself to spring and you meet a raised crucifix, a guard of ash, or a man no longer where he stood. Once you are low or held, the stake comes. While they stand whole they spend their prayers sparingly, and freely once they bleed.
nightborn.journal.vampire.the_eldest.1: At the top of every mountain castle waits the Eldest, the first and oldest of us, with every gift of every bloodline. The living can call it down with four relics and a ritual. It kills them on sight and leaves us be, unless you strike it. Call it yourself and it turns on you. It does not care to be summoned.

nightborn.lore.cellar_ledger.title: Ledger of the Cellar
nightborn.lore.cellar_ledger.page.1: Stock of the cellar, autumn count. Forty bottles, sealed. Eleven casks, of which two are fit for guests and nine are fit for the guests we do not like.
nightborn.lore.cellar_ledger.page.2: The village vintage declines yearly. They eat turnips, they worry, and it can be tasted. I have written to the reeve to suggest more honey and less dread. He has not replied.
nightborn.lore.cellar_ledger.page.3: Note for the household: the bottles sealed with red wax are for the lord's table. The bottles with no wax are also for the lord's table. Kindly stop asking.
nightborn.lore.sunless_diary.title: Four Hundred Years of Evenings
nightborn.lore.sunless_diary.page.1: I have not seen a sunrise in four hundred years. I am told I have missed nothing. The poets who say otherwise are all dead, which I consider the end of the argument.
nightborn.lore.sunless_diary.page.2: The house across the valley has acquired a gramophone. It owns a single record. I have now heard that adagio more often than the man who wrote it.
nightborn.lore.sunless_diary.page.3: I sent a note asking that it be played more softly, or by someone else, or in another country. The reply came back set to music.
nightborn.lore.sunless_diary.page.4: Four hundred years. I gave up the sun without complaint. I will not give up my evenings.
nightborn.lore.coffin_letters.title: Letters Concerning a Coffin
nightborn.lore.coffin_letters.page.1: Cousin. The dark oak coffin in the north vault was promised to me by our late sire, before witnesses, two of whom yet endure. You have slept in it since the spring.
nightborn.lore.coffin_letters.page.2: You write that a promise made before the present king's reign has lapsed. I have outlasted nine kings. I do not recognise lapsing.
nightborn.lore.coffin_letters.page.3: I have measured it. It is a hand too short for you. You sleep with your knees bent out of spite, and the whole house knows it.
nightborn.lore.coffin_letters.page.4: Keep the coffin. I have taken the lid.
nightborn.lore.table_manners.title: On Conduct at Table
nightborn.lore.table_manners.page.1: A guest is greeted before he is tasted. This is the whole of civilisation, and I am weary of repeating it.
nightborn.lore.table_manners.page.2: One does not drink from the neck at table. The wrist is offered, as bread is offered. The neck is for family occasions and for the road.
nightborn.lore.table_manners.page.3: Do not ask a guest's age. If he is young it shames him. If he is old he will tell you, at length, beginning with a siege.
nightborn.lore.table_manners.page.4: Spills are the servants' concern. Your concern is to seem as though you have never spilled anything in your life.
nightborn.lore.hunter_notes.title: Of Hunters: Observations
nightborn.lore.hunter_notes.page.1: They come in bands, at dusk, which they believe to be clever. They carry stakes of plain wood, and whittle them by the fire where anyone might watch.
nightborn.lore.hunter_notes.page.2: The stake is feared more than it deserves by one who stands unhurt. It is the blow that brings one of us down, or finds us already fallen, that ends the matter. Therefore: do not fall.
nightborn.lore.hunter_notes.page.3: The water in their flasks has been prayed over. It burns like noon. I do not know what was said to it, and I do not care to.
nightborn.lore.hunter_notes.page.4: They hang garlic at their tents. It is not the smell that offends. It is the presumption.
nightborn.lore.garlic_complaint.title: A Complaint Against Garlic
nightborn.lore.garlic_complaint.page.1: It is a bulb. I wish that written first, so that the reader may keep his sense of proportion, as I have failed to keep mine.
nightborn.lore.garlic_complaint.page.2: A field of it lies west of the village, and I have gone the long way round for sixty years. The long way adds an hour. I have given that bulb two and a half years of my nights.
nightborn.lore.garlic_complaint.page.3: Its fumes make the strong weak and the weak ridiculous. I have seen an elder of nine centuries sneeze himself out of a window.
nightborn.lore.silver_warning.title: Silver: A Warning to the Young
nightborn.lore.silver_warning.page.1: The young believe silver is a matter of taste, like damask. It is not. A silver blade does not ask your rank.
nightborn.lore.silver_warning.page.2: I once kept a silver service of forty settings. I sold it to a hunter's widow at a fair price. I have regretted the fair price ever since.
nightborn.lore.silver_warning.page.3: If a guest's sword shines whiter than steel ought to, compliment it, and seat him far from the family.
nightborn.lore.fledgling_corvin.title: Regarding the Fledgling Corvin
nightborn.lore.fledgling_corvin.page.1: My lord. The fledgling Corvin was turned eleven nights ago and has already asked which chair will be his. I told him the floor has served many of us well.
nightborn.lore.fledgling_corvin.page.2: He hunts loudly. He was seen in the village twice in one week, and waved. The villagers now mutter, and bolt their doors a full hour earlier.
nightborn.lore.fledgling_corvin.page.3: He asks when he will be an elder. I said: when everyone who remembers this conversation is dust. He has begun a list.
nightborn.lore.hunter_aldric.title: The Matter of the Hunter Aldric
nightborn.lore.hunter_aldric.page.1: We have killed the hunter Aldric three times. I say this without pride, for he does not seem to hold it against us, which is the unsettling part.
nightborn.lore.hunter_aldric.page.2: The first time, he fell from our tower. He returned within the month with a limp and a larger crossbow.
nightborn.lore.hunter_aldric.page.3: The second time, we left him to the wolves. One of the wolves now follows him about.
nightborn.lore.hunter_aldric.page.4: I propose we leave him alone. Not from mercy. I am simply curious to see what finally does it.
nightborn.lore.heart_of_the_house.title: The Heart of the House
nightborn.lore.heart_of_the_house.page.1: Every house of our kind has a heart: the room where the household gathers, and from which the rest was built outward, wing by wing, century by century.
nightborn.lore.heart_of_the_house.page.2: You may find it by the mist. It is thin at our gates and thick at the heart, so that a stranger who can no longer see his own hand may know he has arrived, and is expected.
nightborn.lore.heart_of_the_house.page.3: Visitors remark that the mist is unwelcoming. They are correct. It was a great expense, and it is a comfort to hear that it works.
nightborn.lore.of_the_eldest.title: Of the Eldest
nightborn.lore.of_the_eldest.page.1: All our lines run back to one, and that one endures. We call him the Eldest, because every name he was given has since worn away.
nightborn.lore.of_the_eldest.page.2: He keeps the highest room of the mountain house and does not come down. He has not come down within my memory, which is long, nor my sire's, which was longer.
nightborn.lore.of_the_eldest.page.3: It is said he may be called, with the proper rite at the proper altar. It is not said why anyone would. One does not ring for one's ancestor as one rings for supper.
nightborn.lore.old_blood_fonts.title: The Fonts of Old Blood
nightborn.lore.old_blood_fonts.page.1: At the heart of every house of ours stands a font of old blood: what remains of those who came before us, kept and not wasted. It fills slowly, and twice as slowly when a house stands empty.
nightborn.lore.old_blood_fonts.page.2: It is not for us. One of our own who drinks from it gains nothing, and is thought greedy. It is kept for the living, who drink, sicken, and in time join the family.
nightborn.lore.old_blood_fonts.page.3: A well-fed house will let a quiet stranger walk in and drink. This is called hospitality. The stranger may call it what he likes afterwards, when he is one of us.
nightborn.lore.staff_grievances.title: The Staff's Grievances, Answered
nightborn.lore.staff_grievances.page.1: The thralls have submitted grievances. I did not know they could write. I am told one of them was a clerk, which explains the margins.
nightborn.lore.staff_grievances.page.2: First: the candles. They ask for fewer. No. We keep candles so that we may be seen to ignore them.
nightborn.lore.staff_grievances.page.3: Second: that they be fed at regular hours. Granted. I am not a monster, whatever is said in the village, and on the gate.
nightborn.lore.bat_shape.title: On Taking the Shape of a Bat
nightborn.lore.bat_shape.page.1: The young take the bat's shape for sport. It is a means of travel, like a carriage, and no one should enjoy a carriage that much.
nightborn.lore.bat_shape.page.2: Mind the change back. I have seen a fledgling return to himself above a moat. He was very brave about it afterwards, and very wet.
nightborn.lore.bat_shape.page.3: Do not hang from the rafters in company. It is restful, I grant. It is also how the late Lord Emmerich came to be mistaken for a coat.
nightborn.lore.gallery_portrait.title: The Portrait in the Long Gallery
nightborn.lore.gallery_portrait.page.1: Having no use for mirrors, I sat for a portrait in order to learn what I look like. That was three centuries ago. I am still considering my reply.
nightborn.lore.gallery_portrait.page.2: The painter gave me my mother's chin. I did not have my mother's chin. I had gone to some trouble, in fact, to have nothing of my mother's.
nightborn.lore.gallery_portrait.page.3: It hangs in the long gallery, where guests praise the likeness. I thank them. I have no way of knowing whether they are being kind.
nightborn.lore.church_above.title: Notes on the Church Above
nightborn.lore.church_above.page.1: We have kept the crypt beneath this church since before its tower was raised. The congregation believes the cold comes up from the stone. In a sense it does.
nightborn.lore.church_above.page.2: They sing every seventh morning. They are flat, and the bell is worse. I have lain awake through six hundred years of the same four hymns.
nightborn.lore.church_above.page.3: Still, I would not move. The roof is sound, the neighbours below ground are quiet, and no one has ever thought to look under a church for the likes of us.
nightborn.lore.bone_reckoning.title: A Reckoning of the Bones
nightborn.lore.bone_reckoning.page.1: Counted this winter: nine hundred and four skulls, in good order, facing the door as is proper.
nightborn.lore.bone_reckoning.page.2: Last winter there were nine hundred and five. I have asked the household. Everyone is very surprised, and the fledgling has a new candlestick.
nightborn.lore.cave_defence.title: In Defence of the Cave
nightborn.lore.cave_defence.page.1: My cousins in their castles ask how I can bear to live underground. I ask how they can bear a roof that has, on four occasions, been set alight by the neighbours.
nightborn.lore.cave_defence.page.2: There is no dawn down here. There are no shutters to be barred, no curtains to be trusted, no east. I have not thought about the east in two hundred years.
nightborn.lore.cave_defence.page.3: It drips. I will be honest about the dripping. One grows fond of it, or one goes to live in a castle and is set alight.
nightborn.lore.high_house_winter.title: A Winter in the High House
nightborn.lore.high_house_winter.page.1: The high house was built upon the peak so that no army could reach it. No army has. Nor has the baker, the tailor, or anyone bringing news.
nightborn.lore.high_house_winter.page.2: It has snowed since the equinox. The battlements are white, the stairs are white, and my lord has asked twice whether the snow could be made to fall elsewhere.
nightborn.lore.high_house_winter.page.3: The thralls must be carried up the last mile. They arrive cold, which the household holds against me, as though I had set the mountain here myself.
nightborn.lore.newly_turned.title: Counsel to One Newly Turned
nightborn.lore.newly_turned.page.1: You are hungry, and you will remain so. Do not mistake this for a tragedy. It is an appetite, and appetites are what the living have in place of purpose.
nightborn.lore.newly_turned.page.2: The sun will kill you. I mention it because every fledgling believes, privately, that he will be the exception. I have swept up a great many exceptions.
nightborn.lore.newly_turned.page.3: Sleep in your coffin by day. Not near it. Not on it. The lid is not a suggestion.
nightborn.lore.newly_turned.page.4: In a hundred years you will be tolerable. In three hundred, you may speak at table.
